newsitem.title: UK: Dollar firmer in late Europe as mark edges lower.
newsitem.headline: Dollar firmer in late Europe as mark edges lower.

text.p: The dollar was firmer on the mark and yen by late European trade, recovering from its earlier lows but keeping within tight afternoon ranges.
The mark found strength early in the session from the fading prospect of further German interest rate cuts as well as today's Swedish repo rate cut and Wednesday's Italian rate cut.
But by late trade, some of the mark's firmness in Europe had eroded and its retreat from a session high against the yen also helped underpin the dollar.
"We've seen good two-way business today with the bias towards a higher dollar," said a Japanese bank dealer.
At 1528 GMT, the dollar was trading at 1.5215/20 marks compared with 1.5222/27 late Wednesday in Europe.
Wednesday's comments by senior Bundesbank officials that German interest rates were at correct levels and likely to remain steady dashed expectations of further German cuts.
This steady rate policy was underlined by the Bundesbank's decision to keep rates on hold at today's council meeting.

The dimming prospect of lower German rates pressured the dollar in early trade but it managed to find strong support at 1.5180 marks, a level dealers said is providing a good base for its current trading range.
Analysts said, however, that although rates are probably at their lowest levels, a rate rise is very unlikely given the modest pace of recovery in Germany's economy.
Today's West German preliminary consumer price data for October also showed a benign inflation outlook with CPI unchanged from September and up 1.5 percent for the year.
Although the mark had given up some of its early gains on the European currencies, it was still firm against the yen.
"Mark/yen has been bid up today on good U.S. fund buying but heavy offers at 74.20 will take a lot to get through," said the Japanese bank dealer.
By 1601 GMT, the mark stood at 74.15/17 yen after touching a 44-month high of 74.30 in overnight trade. It was trading at 74.22/25 late Wednesday in Europe.
Technical analysts said the mark would have to break tough resistance at 74.50 yen before targeting 75.25, the July 1991 low which underpinned the cross until February 1993.

The dollar was steady against the yen but was finding it tough to clear the 113 yen level today after Wednesday's 33-month high of 113.12. The dollar was trading at 112.81/91 yen in late trade today compared with 112.93/98 on Wednesday.
